description: DDL adapter for Codex (the protocol's implementations under hosts/codex/). The rule against mutation without approval always applies. From a prepared report or Git review in the record, a question carrying its ID, or a line-initial +++DDL_REPORT, until submitted human input, the gate guards only tool calls covered by the runtime tool hooks; it reads no reasoning item. Its catch-all matcher permits known safe reads, the gate's own report preparation, the prepared question unchanged, input-free polling, and bounded literal shell reads; mutating calls, unknown tools, worker follow-ups, and a dispatched question lacking the pending ID or differing from the prepared one are denied on those paths. The processor decides whether an actual submitted answer approves the current report and scope. Turn termination remains an instruction; running processes and hook-bypassing transports are outside this guard. The protocol's implementations under hosts/codex/ record the dispatch coverage and the human-input boundary; the asynchronous-transcript and fail-open limits are in the maintainer reference (Runtime boundaries). In a DDL project (instruction file with the → DDL-PROTOCOL line), SessionStart injects design.md when present. Project-local configuration requires project trust; user-level hooks are independent of project trust. Review new or changed hooks in /hooks when the runtime requests it. One decision serves PreToolUse and PermissionRequest. PreToolUse never returns allow (Codex refuses it there) and keeps every deny, also an edit, command class or machine outside every active grant, an exit behind ssh, and any recognized write of the ledger files. PermissionRequest returns allow only for a call inside an active grant (recorded from the approved plan's question, before its expiry, while no STOP is pending and the record is readable; never for a protected file such as the adapters' files, the instruction files or the notebook) or for a commit or push matched to its answered Git review, and never for a call asking for escalated sandbox permissions, so Codex asks nothing more; otherwise it prints nothing, and it never sets updatedInput, updatedPermissions or interrupt. Every other call, including other exits, keeps Codex's own approval policy; whether its own rules still apply after the PermissionRequest allow is unchecked. Independently of STOP, the hook denies recognized static noncanonical push forms in confirmation-enabled modes. The hook never rewrites commands and does not inspect arbitrary scripts or aliases. The rules live in the skills and protocol and remain instructions where the adapter is absent or cannot enforce them. Ordinary Git commit/push calls additionally require the prepared content review matched to the actual native submission and Git snapshot, even while STOP is open or native permission prompts are suppressed. An unreadable or mismatched Git review denies recognized calls. Runtime-level hook failures and timeouts remain outside that guarantee. After a commit allowed inside a grant, PostToolUse compares the new commit's paths with the grant and logs any path outside it as a warning that the next push review shows; it decides nothing.
